question: What fish profile names does the official Asid Gulf guide document, and what can this source support for regional coverage?

studyScopeAsReported.geographicScope: The guide is titled for Asid Gulf. Its introduction situates the gulf in the Visayan Sea and describes it across Regions V, VI and VII; this does not mean the guide is a complete checklist for those regions.
studyScopeAsReported.fisheryContext: The guide documents common finfish in commercial and municipal catches. Its introduction reports NSAP work in Asid Gulf beginning in 2007 and identifies landing centers at Milagros, Balud and Placer.
studyScopeAsReported.perProfileFieldPeriod: No field date or capture event is attached to each profile in the reviewed guide pages.

evidenceBoundary: The 86 rows are a transcription of profile names only (scientific, English and local names); line wrapping was normalized to spaces. No species descriptions, photographs or extended text were copied.
A fish-guide profile is not a dated occurrence, a voucher-backed observation, a capture coordinate, or a proof of current presence or abundance at a specific site.
The guide is limited to its Asid Gulf fishery scope. It is not a complete checklist for Region V, VI or VII, all of Masbate, other marine waters, rivers, lakes, reservoirs, wetlands or estuaries.
The guide does not establish diet, catchability, bait effectiveness, native or introduced status, current legal access, or safety.
Common and local names are retained as printed source claims; they are not taxonomic matches or standardized vernacular names.

The 2019 guide states that all rights are reserved but allows reproduction/dissemination for educational or other non-commercial purposes with full acknowledgment; resale and commercial reproduction are prohibited. Public-app reuse remains unapproved pending a separate scope and rights review.

disposition.reason: GBIF returned 86 ordered name-matching results. Nine names need manual review because of a variant, synonym usage or alternative candidates; the remaining machine matches are still candidates, not independent verification or occurrence evidence.

nextAction: Manually reconcile the nine flagged names with current fish taxonomic authorities and source authorship; preserve the guide names unchanged. Then continue the separate regional freshwater/brackish/coastal source sweep by named waterbody.

NFRDI report identifies the Asid Gulf guide as one of the BFAR Region V/NFRDI joint NSAP fish guides.
